description: Hi! I'm an 18-year-old solo developer participating in the Flame in Freefall challenge. I built a web app to visualize 1g vs 0g flame behavior and explore NASA microgravity fire datasets (FLEX, BASS-II, SAME-2, SAFFIRE-II) with an interactive Q&A tool. Working as a solo team for this project.
summary:
Flame in Freefall: Microgravity Combustion Explorer is an interactive web app I built to make NASA's microgravity fire-safety research visual, simple, and easy to verify.
On Earth (1g), gravity creates upward airflow that pulls fresh oxygen into tall, sooty flames. In space (0g), buoyancy disappears—flames become spherical shells, smoke particles clump 2x larger over 12 minutes (SAME-2), and gentle cabin airflow lets acrylic (PMMA) burn down to ~13.5% O2 (BASS-II), below Earth's 15.4% limit.
My app brings this NASA data to life through four tools:
1. 1g vs 0g Flame Simulator: A side-by-side HTML5 Canvas visualizer comparing Earth flames against microgravity chambers with live gravity, oxygen, droplet size, and pressure controls.
2. NASA Telemetry & d² Explorer: Interactive charts and searchable tables from FLEX (245 droplet burns), BASS-II (Cabin Screening Check), SAME-2 (smoke aging), and SAFFIRE-II (Cygnus duct burns), plus custom CSV upload.
3. Fire Safety & Earth Engines: Compares ISS (0g), Lunar (0.16g), and Martian (0.38g) fire behavior alongside clean-engine modeling (PSI-62).
4. Grounded AI Specialist: A server-side Gemini Q&A tool locked strictly to loaded NASA files, separating measured file evidence from general physics to prevent hallucinations.
Built with Google AI Studio, Gemini API, and ChatGPT using open NASA NTRS/PSI datasets and live ISS telemetry (NORAD 25544). Licensed under Apache-2.0; no official NASA logos used.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Flame in Freefall: Microgravity Combustion Explorer is an interactive web app that helps students, educators, and researchers visualize how fire behaves in space (0g) compared to Earth (1g). It features four core tools: (1) a side-by-side HTML5 Canvas simulator comparing Earth buoyant flames with spherical microgravity flames across custom gravity, oxygen, droplet size, and pressure settings; (2) interactive charts and searchable tables built from NASA FLEX (245 droplet burns), BASS-II (Cabin Screening Check), SAME-2 (smoke particle aging), and SAFFIRE-II (Cygnus duct tests), plus local CSV upload; (3) planetary fire-safety comparisons for ISS, Moon, and Mars; and (4) a server-side Grounded AI Specialist that answers questions strictly from active NASA datasets with exact file citations.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Critical NASA microgravity fire data is normally locked inside dense technical PDFs, while standard AI chatbots often invent unverified numbers. My platform turns raw NASA tables into clear visual insights for spacecraft fire safety and Earth clean-combustion education while preventing AI hallucinations.

Tools, Languages & Creative Design
Built solo using React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, and a Node.js/Express backend. Developed with Google AI Studio and powered at runtime by the Google Gemini API (@google/genai), with Google Gemini and ChatGPT used for brainstorming and structuring notes. To keep the app accessible and accurate, I added a 3-step onboarding guide, plain-language finding cards, custom people-free SVG hardware schematics, and an Apache-2.0 open license (no official NASA logos used).
